question_text:
Equation is given by:

$$\frac{m_{0} q^{4}}{2\left(4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}\right)^{2} \hbar^{2}}$$

where $m_{0}=9.11 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ is the mass of an electron, $q=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ is the charge of an electron, $\varepsilon_{0}=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}$ is the permittivity of free space, and $\hbar=1.05 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \cdot \mathrm{~s}$ is the reduced Planck constant. 

Calculate the its value.The unit of the answer is eV.
response:
The expression is the Rydberg energy. Substituting the given values:

$$E=\frac{m_0 q^4}{2(4\pi\varepsilon_0)^2\hbar^2}\approx 2.19\times10^{-18}\,\text{J}$$

Converting to electron-volts using $1\,\text{eV}=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$:

$$E \approx \frac{2.189\times10^{-18}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}\approx 13.68\,\text{eV}$$

This is the ionization energy of hydrogen (Rydberg energy), consistent with the well-known value of $13.6\,\text{eV}$.

$$\boxed{13.68}$$
